steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: The Issue Evaluation is Section A of AQA GCSE Geography Paper 3 (Geographical Applications). It tests your ability to use geographical skills, critical thinking, and knowledge to analyse a contemporary geographical issue. You receive pre-release resources 12 weeks before the exam.

steps.title: Step-by-Step Approach
steps.body: Read all resources carefully at least twice Annotate key information, patterns, and links between resources Identify the geographical issue and its key components Locate the issue spatially - use maps to understand place context Connect the resources to your wider geographical knowledge Evaluate the reliability and bias of each source

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Stakeholders are individuals, groups, or organisations that have an interest in or are affected by a geographical issue. Different stakeholders often have conflicting views because they have different priorities, values, and interests.

steps.title: Exam Technique
steps.body: When asked about stakeholder viewpoints: (1) Identify who the stakeholders are; (2) Explain their specific interest/concern; (3) Use evidence from the resource booklet; (4) Show how and why viewpoints conflict; (5) Consider which viewpoints are better supported by evidence.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Why is it important to consider the reliability of sources in the pre-release booklet? | Explain why stakeholders often have conflicting viewpoints about geographical issues. | Describe the PEEL structure and explain how it helps you answer evaluation questions.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Source reliability is important because different sources may be biased or have limited perspective. A newspaper article may use emotive language or omit facts; a developer's report may emphasise bene | Stakeholders have conflicting viewpoints because they have different priorities and interests. Local residents may prioritise quality of life and property values, while developers prioritise profit an | PEEL stands for Point, Evidence, Explain, Link. You start by stating your argument (Point), then support it with data from the resource booklet (Evidence), then show how the evidence supports your arg

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Study the pre-release booklet thoroughly - annotate it, make notes, discuss it in class You cannot bring your annotated booklet into the exam - a clean copy is provided Always refer to specific figures and sources from the booklet (e.g. "Figure 3 shows...") For the 9-mark question, you MUST take a position - don't be indecisive Use geographical terminology correctly (sustainability, stakeholder, mitigation, trade-off) Consider short-term AND long-term impacts in your evaluations Remember SPaG marks (3 marks) - write in full sentences, use paragraphs, spell correctly Practice timing: spend about 60 minutes on Section A
